title: Avatar Properties
content: ### Objective Set the Avatar's properties, such as skin style, eye direction, skin friction, and color of body elements. ### Location 3D Window ▶ Select Avatar ▶ Property Editor ### ### Operation Set the Avatar's properties. When you select an avatar, its properties appear in the property window. **Avatar Properties** **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Information** | **Name** | Enter a name and an item number for the avatar. **Size** | Lists the size Preset chosen from the Avatar Editor. **Body Styling** | **Skin Style** (Ver. 2025.0) | Set the appearance of the avatar from presets or Customize You can manually set the color of hair, skin, underwear, eyebrows, eyes, and lips by clicking the Style Configurator button on the right. **Eye Control** (Ver. 2025.0) | **Horizontal** | Adjust the position of the avatar's eyes horizontally. **Vertical** | Adjust the position of the avatar's eyes vertically. **Surface** | **Skin Offset** | Adjust the distance between the avatar and the garment. Since the avatar and the garment consist of meshes, a very high particle distance and a low Skin Offset value can cause the avatar to protrude out from under the garment. To prevent this, the default Skin Offset value is set to 3mm, which is the proper value for creating a garment. When you fit your garment accurately or create a fitted garment, lower the value of the Skin Offset. ※ Note: Leave the default value until you almost finish your garment, as the simulation will slow down when you lower the Skin Offset of the avatar and the Particle Distance of the garment. **Static Friction** | The friction setting when a garment is in a stationary position. **Kinetic Friction** | The friction setting when a garment is moving. **Soft Body Simulation** (Ver. 2024.0 and above) | Apply a deformable body simulation to express skin elasticity When recording animations, Defualt Adult Avatar animations with soft body simulation are recorded separately and can be exported to Alembic Cache. For other formats, they will only be exported based on the current frame. ※ Note: * When Soft Body Simulation is on, a button is displayed in the bottom right corner of the 3D window to indicate its activation status. * Avatar-type objects that are not rigged can also be simulated. (2025.1) * NVIDIA GPU is supported starting from version 2025.2. **Soft Body Stiffness** | Min - Max: 5,000 - 10,000 The smaller the value, the smoother the simulation. **Divide Mesh** (Ver. 2025.0) | Subdivides the mesh of the avatars to smooth the surface of the avatar. Values are between 1 and 3. Use this feature only when necessary. The denser you set the mesh, the slower the simulation will run. E.g., This works best when you drape a fitted garment, such as leggings, since a low-density avatar mesh may be visible. **Material (Selected)** | Set the [Material](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358364198425) of the selected part of the avatar. For Example: select the eyes and adjust color, base color map, etc. **Miscellaneous** | **Mesh Type** | Indicates the type of selected avatar mesh. **Element Count** | Indicates the number of points in the selected mesh. **Avatar Properties (ver. 2024.2)** **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Information** | **Name** | Enter a name and an item number of the avatar. **Model** | You can change the type of avatar. **Surface** | **Skin Offset** | Adjust the distance between the avatar and the garment. Since the avatar and the garment consist of the meshes, a very high value of particle distance and low value of Skin Offset can cause the avatar to protrude out from under the garment. To prevent this, the default Skin Offset value is set to 3mm, which is the proper value for creating a garment. When you fit your garment accurately or create a fitted garment, lower the value of the Skin Offset. ※ Note: Leave the default value until you almost finish your garment, since the simulation is being slow when you lower the Skin Offset of the avatar and the Particle Distance of the garment. **Static Friction** | The friction when a garment is in stationary position. **Kinetic Friction** | The friction when a garment is moving. **Soft Body Simulation** (ver. 2024.0) | Apply deformable body simulation to express skin elasticity When recording animations, avatar animations with soft body simulation are recorded separately and can be exported to Alembic Cache. For other formats, they will only be exported based on the current frame. ※ Note: When Soft Body Simulation is on, a button is displayed in the bottom right corner of the 3D window to indicate its activation status. **Soft Body Stiffness** | Min - Max: 5,000 - 10,000 The smaller the value, the smoother the simulation. **Material**(Selected) | Set the [Material](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358364198425) of the avatar. **Miscellaneous** | **Mesh Type** | Indicates the type of avatar mesh. **Element Count** | Indicates the number of points in the mesh. **Smooth Avatar** | **Smooth** | Toggles the Smooth option on or off. If the option is on, the mesh on the avatar's surface will be divided as set in 'Division Level'. **Division Level** | Can be split by a factor of 1 to 5. **Soft Body Simulation (ver. 2024.0)** **Soft Body for Custom Avatars (ver. 2025.1)**
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for users to customize their avatar's properties, including appearance, eye control, friction settings, and soft body simulation, enhancing the overall user experience in the 3D environment.

title: 3D File (FBX) Import/Export
content: ### Objective Import a file's Geometry, Material, Joint, and Camera Animation information in the FBX file format (ver2.2.0). ### Location #### Import FBX Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ FBX #### Export FBX Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ FBX ### Operation #### Import FBX 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ FBX → The Open File window appears. 2. Select the desired file and click OK. → The Import FBX window appears. 3. Select the settings and click OK. → The FBX file is imported based on the setting. Load Type | Open | All existing objects will be removed, leaving the imported FBX file only. ---|---|--- Add | Add a FBX file, keeping the existing objects. Auto Create Fitting Suit | For humanoid avatars only, a Fitting Suit is automatically created in the import process. Object Type | Avatar | Import a FBX file as an Avatar type. \- Objects imported as an Avatar type can be muti-selected. Trim | Import a FBX file as a Trim type. \- The object will pass through the clothing while Simulation is on, as the Trim type cannot collide with clothing. \- Set the collide option for a Trim type on the Property Editor by toggling on the Collision check-box. \- Select an trim object and toggle on the Glue icon on the gizmo to attach the object to clothing. \- Toggle on the Scale icon on the gizmo to scale the size of an object. Scene & Props | Import FBX file in Scene & Props format. \- You can use the Collision menu in the property window. Object | Camera | Toggles whether the Camera data or Camera Animation data is imported Joint Animation | Toggles whether the Joint Animation date is imported. Cache Animation (mc) | Toggles whether the Cache Animation data is imported. Automatically Add Arrangement Points | For humanoid avatars only, arrangement points are automatically generated in the import process. Scale | Input the Specific Value or Choose Measure. Axis Conversion | Modifying Object's Axis direction.(ver. 12.2) Translation | Align Bottom to Ground | When an object is placed below the ground, toggle on Align Bottom to Ground check-box to place the object imported above ground. Option | Move Garment to Start Position | Move the garment to the starting frame of the imported motion. #### Export FBX 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ FBX → The Save File window appears. 2. Designate the file saving path and file name, and then click OK. → The Export OBJ window appears. 3. Select the settings as needed and click OK. → The file is exported as a FBX file based on the setting. Object | Select an Avatar (ver 6.1) Select the avatar to be exported. ※ Note: The selected avatar is saved with its rigging data. You can exclude it as desired. Select All Avatars (ver. 12.2) \- All existing avatars will be exported. ---|--- Single Object Exports the selected object as a single object. | Multiple Objects Exports the selected object as multiple objects. Un-Weld Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. ※ Thickness exports for quad meshes available beginning version 2.3.0 (ver2.3.0). | Weld Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. Weld Selected Pattern: Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns (ver2.3.0). Thin Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. ※ Note: * When an object is exported as a single object, its texture is exported as a whole even when its sides (front, back, and side) have different textures (ver5.0.0.) | Thick Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. ※ Note: * The thickness can be exported when Pattern Mesh is Quadrangular (ver2.3.0.) * Each side's texture is exported individually when an object's front, back, side have different textures (ver5.0.0.) Combined UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. ※Note: Unified Texture (ver3.1.0). Export multiple layers of texture information as a single UV texture information. | Image File | Designate file saving path and file name. Add numbers behind the file name as below: ‘File Name_0’, ‘File Name_1’. ---|--- Texture Size | Width and Height will be saved in a fixed ratio. Allowance: 512 ~ 8192 Pixel Fill Texture Seams | Expands the scope of the texture having its boundary line as the standard. Allowance: 0 ~ 15 mm When you type in values, preview will show in the 2D Window. Animation | Joint Animation: Saves the animation data that was originally imported with the FBX file. Cache Animation (MC): Saves the cache data along with the recorded Garment Animation. Scale | Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered or the desired unit from “Unit in file to import” is selected. Axis Conversion | Changes the directions of each axis of the object. Animation | Entire Area (saves all of the recorded garment animation.) | Play Area Only (saves only the play area garment animation.) File | File Type: Select between Binary or Ascii file type. * Binary: The file is saved in binary and cannot be opened by users. * Ascii: The file is saved as text and can be opened by users. Relative Texture Image File Path: Saves the texture image name without a texture image file path. Texture images are saved in the same folder as the FBX file, for automatic import. Absolute Texture Image File Path: Saves the file path that contained the texture images as the texture file path. If the texture image file path is changed, texture images cannot be imported. Save With Texture Files (.zip): Exports the .obj file, .mtl file, and texture images used in the garment as one compressed file when exporting animation. ※ Note: 1. FBX SDK 2020 version is available. (ver 10) * Only Joint that was imported as FBX to Marvelous Designer can be exported as FBX. 2. Import/Export FBX with multiple avatars (ver 12.2) * Multiple avatars can be imported or exported simultaneously using the FBX file format. 3. Export FBX with Material Names (Ver 2025.0) * Material Names are now synchronized exported with the FBX.
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for importing and exporting FBX files, enabling users to manage geometry, materials, joint animations, and camera animations efficiently within their projects.

Portrait or Landscape Width | Type in desired Width for the image. Height | Type in desired Height for the image. Unit | Set the above Width and Height Units of measurement: Pixels, Inches, Millimeters, Centimeters Resolution (ppi) | Assign Resolution for the image. Pixels | Generates the pixel dimensions based on the input properties above (You cannot affect the numbers in this window). #### **Options** Show Lines Select All | Select all line types to be included in the exported image. ---|--- Graphic Lines | Include the box that surrounds the graphic. Internal Lines | Include red internal lines in image. Pattern Outlines | Include the Black Pattern outline. Symmetric/ Instance Lines | Include the connecting line for instance or symmetric connector lines. Show Images Select All | Select which images will be included in the exported image. ---|--- Fabric Texture | Include the applied Fabric texture. Graphic | Include any applied Graphic styles. title: Auto Fitting
content: Create Fitting Suit Auto Fitting & Re-Target Draping/Re-Drape 3D Arrangement (ver. 2025.0) Show Avatar Fitting Suit (Above ver. 11) Show Garment Fitting Suit (Above ver. 11) * * * ## Create Fitting Suit ### Objective Create a Fitting Suit for a custom avatar for Auto Fitting. Create a Fitting Suit Reference Line along the avatar surface and apply Fitting Suit. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶****[**Avatar Editor**](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358128221337) ▶ Create Fitting Suit (ver. 2025.0) Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Create Fitting Suit (ver. 10 - 2024.2) 3D Toolbar ▶ Create Fitting Suit (ver. 10-2024.2) ### Operation 1\. Load your custom avatar. 2\. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location for your version. 3\. Create Fitting Suit Reference Line following the guide of dialogue and mouse pointer. → When you have finished creating the lines, the preview of the Fitting Suit appears. 4\. After creating all reference lines, press Apply button. → Fitting Suit is simulated on the avatar. 5\. Press Save button to save the avatar. → It is saved as an avatar file (.avt) including Fitting Suit data. ※Note If you do not want to create symmetry, turn off Symmetry settings. If you want to recreate the reference line, select the reference line in the dialogue and press the Delete button. * * * ## Auto Fitting & Re-Target Draping/Re-Drape 3D Arrangement (ver. 2025.0) ### Objective **Auto Fitting** Automatically adjust the size of your garment to your custom avatar and simulate the garment. **Re-Target Draping / Re-Drape 3D Arrangement (ver. 2025.0)** Simulate garment on your custom avatar. (This function maintains its original size) ### Location **Auto Fitting** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Fitting ▶ Auto Fitting 2D Toolbar ▶ Auto Fitting **Re-Target Draping / Re-Drape 3D Arrangement (ver. 2025.0)** Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Re-Target Draping/Re-Drape 3D Arrangement (2025.0) 3D Toolbar ▶ Re-Target Draping/Re-Drape 3D Arrangement (2025.0) ### Operation 1\. Load the avatar which has completed the Create Fitting Suit process. 2\. Add the garment which has Fitting Suit data. \- The garment simulated on the avatar provided by Marvelous Designer (Marvelous Designer 9.5 or above) \- The garment simulated on the avatar having Fitting Suit data after doing Create Fitting Suit. 3\. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 4\. Adjust the below options as needed in the popup window, and click OK. Option | Description ---|--- **Maintain Pattern Curvature (%)** | Set the extent of deformation of pattern curvature. * Higher values will deform only the size of the pattern while preserving the existing curvature, while lower values will deform both the size and curvature of the pattern. **Maintain Graphic Size** | ON | Graphics maintain their size after auto fitting OFF | The graphic is automatically resized based on the size changes of the patters. **Maintain Texture Size** | ON | Textures maintain their size after auto fitting OFF | The Texture is automatically resized based on the size changes of the patters. **Maintain Topology** | ON | The topological structure is maintained after auto fitting. ※ Auto Fitting requires all pattern meshes to be fully synchronized to avoid remeshing during simulation. If the mesh is not synchronized, Auto Fitting will attempt to remesh the patterns, which means it cannot preserve the current topology. The simplest way to synchronize the mesh is to run a simulation, and you may need to readjust the UV map afterward. OFF | The topological structure is automatically remeshed and modified during Auto Fitting. → Auto Fitting The size of the garment is automatically adjusted and the garment is simulated on your custom avatar. → Re-Drape 3D Arrangement (ver. 2025.0) The garment maintains its size, UV, textures and is simulated on your custom avatar. ※Note * Before you press the Menu button, increase the particle distance of the 3D garment, which will help this function run faster. * Before you press Menu button, change the property of the 3D garment to its default, which will help this function run efficiently. * * * ## Show Avatar Fitting Suit (Above ver. 11) Please follow the below to see the details of an avatar fitting suit View icons on the 3D window ▶ Avatar Display ▶ Show Avatar Fitting Suit * * * ## Show Garment Fitting Suit (Above ver. 11) Please follow the below to see the details of a garment fitting suit View icons on the 3D window ▶ 3D Garment Display ▶ Show Garment Fitting Suit
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for creating and applying a Fitting Suit for custom avatars and garments in the latest version of 3D modeling software.

title: [MODE] UV EDITOR: Bake Textures
content: ### Objective Bake selected texture. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ UV Editor Mode ▶ Tool Bar ▶ Bake Textures Tool ### Operation 1. Follow the path indicated in the Location above. → The Bake Textures setting window will be displayed. 2. Set values according to the table below. **Bake Textures Detail Setting Table** Saving Path | Click folder button to set the file path and save path. Select PNG either JPEG file format. With PNG save option, the background will be transparent. With JPEG save option, the background will be black. ---|--- Size (pixels) | Set the size of the image to be saved. Images are stored in squares of the same horizontal and vertical size. Fill Texture Seams (ver. 2024.1) | Set how many pixels to pad the UV shells by. Min: 1 ~ Max: 256 Pixels Infinite Seams (ver. 2024.1) | UV Seam Padding is extended to infinity. UV area | 0-1 (Default) | Save default 0 to 1 tile. Fill Texture Seams | The outline is filled with texture as you enter the pixels. Texture type | Select texture types to be saved. 3\. After setting the details, click the "Save" button at the bottom. → The image is baked and saved to the path you set. ※ Note: * When baking, the seamline normal map will be baked together. (ver.10) * The UV map of the OBJ topstitch used in a garment is also provided. (ver.11) * UV padding pixel value can be adjusted using Fill Texture Seams value. title: GoZ for Marvelous Designer
content: GoZ Install Run GoZ from Marvelous Designer Run GoZ from ZBrush * * * ## ## Objective GoZ allows direct Import and Export of objects between Marvelous Designer and ZBrush. ## GoZ Install Download the installer using the links bellow. * [**Latest GoZ installer for Windows**](https://s3.amazonaws.com/s3.md.web.upload/marvelousdesigner/GoZ_for_Marvelous_Designer_Windows_1.0.0.zip) * [**Latest GoZ installer for MacOS**](https://s3.amazonaws.com/s3.md.web.upload/marvelousdesigner/GoZ_for_Marvlous_Designer_macOS_1.0.0.zip) ※ Note: * The above GoZ installer works with Marvelous Designer (ver. 2024.2 and above) and is compatible with ZBrush 2022 and later. * To access archived version of GoZ for Marvelous Designer 2024.1 and below (for Windows), please download the installer from the link below: * [**[Archived] GoZ installer (Windows)**](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47657221196313) **Install GoZ for Marvelous Designer from ZBrush** 1. Unzip the downloaded zip folder (md_goz_app_[OperatingSystem]_[VersionNumber]), then install GoZ to ZBrush by moving the contents in \MarvelousDesigner\ folder to the following directory: * * Window default directory path: C:\Users\Public\Pixologic\GoZApps\MarvelousDesigner\ * MacOS default directory path: /Users/Shared/Pixologic/GoZApps/MarvelousDesigner/ * ※ Note: For MacOS, after moving the contents in \MarvelousDesigner\ folder to the directory above, go into MarvelousDesigner folder. Please unzip GoZBrushToMarvelousDesigner and GoZInitMarvelousDesigner. 2. After you unzip the "MarvelousDesigner" folder to GoZApps folder, run ZBrush. 3. Go to ZBrush Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ GoZ ▶ path to MarvelousDesigner. 4. In the list displayed, click the version of Marvelous Designer you will be using. 5. If a Security Warning pop-up window appears ▶ click Run. 6. Click 'Install' Button to start GoZ Marvelous Designer installation. ※ Note: * Please Click Replace if file already exist in the GoZApps\MarvelousDesigner folder. * If you have multiple versions of Marvelous Designer installed, please note that the newly revamped GoZ for Marvelous Designer is only available for Marvelous Designer version 2024 and above. * You can verify that the path to the Marvelous Designer executable file is correct by checking in the GoZ_Config.txt file located in the GoZApps\MarvelousDesigner folder. **Reinstall GoZ for Marvelous Designer from ZBrush** 1. Preform Force Reinstall by going to ZBrush Main menu ▶ Preferences ▶ GoZ ▶ Force Reinstall 2. In the list of GoZ enabled application, select Marvelous Designer. 3. Click 'Install' Button to start GoZ Marvelous Designer installation 4. If a Security Warning pop-up window appears, click Run. ※ Note: To ensure GoZ plugin is working properly with Marvelous Designer, please keep the default name for Marvelous Designer application as it is, and do not modify its name. * * * ## Run GoZ from Marvelous Designer After installing GoZ for Marvelous Designer, you can directly export Garments, Avatars, Trims and Scene and Props from Marvelous Designer with the Run GoZ menu. #### **Location** Main Menu ▶ GoZ ▶ Export to ZBrush #### **Operation** 1. Make sure Path to Marvelous Designer is correctly setup with the version of Marvelous Designer in use in ZBrush. 2. Select elements in the scene (Avatar/Garment/Trim/SceneAndProps) to be exported to ZBrush. 3. Go to Main Menu ▶ GoZ and select Export to ZBrush. 4. In the pop-up window, in Object tabs, you can add and remove scene elements to export. 5. Set export setting and click OK button. 6. Go to ZBrush, drag in the 3D window. 7. In Subtool, you can find Patterns + Trim become a single tool, scene and prop become a single tool, and each avatar becomes a tool of its own. 8. PolyGroups are automatically assigned: * * Pattern: split per pattern shapes. * Avatar: split per component. * Trim: split per Trim object. * Scene and Prop: split per Scene and Prop. #### Export to ZBrush Settings Object | Select All Patterns * Select/Deselect all Patterns. * Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right. Select All Avatars * Select/Deselect all Avatars/Objects. * Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right. Select All Trims * Select/Deselect all Trims. * Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right. Select All Scene and Props * Select/Deselect all Scene and Props. * Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right. ---|--- #### Unweld Exports Vertex(points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts as multiple objects. | #### Weld Combines Vertex (points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts together as one point. #### Thin Ensures thickness is not exported to Geometry even if the value is increased beforehand. | #### Thick Exports thickness value to Geometry. Basic | Scale | Adjusts scale of file being exported with a unit of measurements. Scale % | Works on top of the unit of measurement above, scale by specific percentage value. * Reset: Reset all settings to Default. ※ Note: * For Avatar and Scene and Prop, selecting a part of an object will have the corresponding object in the object list to be selected. * Selecting only the body of an avatar will result in the entire avatar being selected in the Export to ZBrush dialog. * * * ## Run GoZ from ZBrush You can directly export object to Marvelous Designer from ZBrush through GoZ. #### **Location** Tool ▶ ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438736204697) #### **Operation** 1. Set Import Settings in Marvelous Designer from Main Menu ▶ GoZ ▶ Import Settings 2. Under Tool window, make sure Marvelous Designer is set as the current GoZ enabled application by clicking the "R" button shown in the image above.![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438736364825) 3. Click GoZ button to export currentSubTool to 'GoZ' enabled application, or use the shortcut Ctrl+G 4. Click All button to export all SubTools to 'GoZ' enabled application, or use the shortcut Ctrl+Shift+G 5. Click Visible button to export visible SubTools to 'GoZ' enabled application. 6. Once the object is exported by GoZ, you can see mesh are imported to Marvelous Designer based on Import Setting #### GoZ Import Settings Basic | Load Type | Open | All existing objects will be removed, leaving the imported file only. ---|---|---|--- Add | Add files and keep the existing objects. Object Type | Avatar | Import file as an Avatar type. \- Objects imported as an Avatar type can be muti-selected. Trim | Import file as Trim type. \- For more information on Trim Type, check out [Trim Properties](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358187139609) Page Garment | Import an Object as Simulation ready Garment, physical properties can be adjusted from the property editor. Scene and Props | Import file as Scene & Props. \- For more information on Scene & Props, check out [Scene and Props Properties](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358290160921) Page Scale | Adjusts scale of file being exported with a unit of measurements. Scale % | Works on top of the unit of measurement above, scale by specific percentage value. content: ### Objective Convert synchronized 3D Garments into quadrangular or triangular mesh structures. ※Note: Please refer to the below explanation on different usages of Quadrangular Mesh versus Triangular Mesh. content: OBJ Topstitch Texture Topstitch ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438090016537) ## Register OBJ Topstitch ### **Objective** Save custom OBJ files as a Topstitch in a *.sst format file type. ### **Location** Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Style Window ▶ Default Topstitch Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Style Window ▶ Default Topstitch Viewport Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown menu ▶ Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Style Window ▶ Default Topstitch ### **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Default Topstitch → Properties of the selected Topstitch appear in the Property Editor. 2. Please check that your OBJ meets the requirements below before attempting to register an OBJ as a Topstitch. * Position the face of an OBJ towards the Y-axis. * Position the contact point of an OBJ where it should be attached to 3D garments at 0,0,0 (x,y,z) coordinates. * The unit of OBJs must be in mm. 3. Select the button on the right of OBJ to load your custom Topstitch ![Screenshot 2025-04-24 152353.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438104147097) 4. Select the button on the right of OBJ to load your custom Topstitch. ![Screenshot 2025-04-24 152425.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438121155225) 5. Press OK ※Recommended: Please maintain the number of vertices of an OBJ below 1000 to avoid speed issues. The distance between an OBJ and the ground should be 0. (You can adjust the distance in Marvelous Designer) ## ![Screenshot 2025-04-24 152425.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438121155225)![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438090016537) ## Register Texture Topstitch ### **Objective** Save customized Topstitch object or texture files in a *.sst format file. ### **Location** Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Default Topstitch ### **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Default Topstitch → Properties of the selected Topstitch appear in the Property Editor. 2. Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Type and select Texture from the drop-down menu. 3. Under the Material section, select the same structured Topstitch as the one customized. 4. Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Texture and click the Topstitch image icon or the Search button. → The Open file window appears. 5. Find the path to the customized images and select the one only with the name of Topstitch (ex. "zigzag.png") and click Open. → The program automatically saves all five images in a *.sst file according to the defined naming rule. → The image is loaded in actual size, which is approximately 2cm. It may look bigger than other preset Topstitches. 6. Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Preset and enter the desired value in the Stitch Width menu (ex. 5mm) to adjust its size. 7. On the top right of the Property Editor, there is a Save button. Select to save. → The Save file window appears. 8. Enter the desired name and location and save. → The Topstitch is now saved in the *.sst file format. ※ Note: Topstitches are classified into two different types depending on the presence or absence of the Stitch Width property. For example, when adding zigzag-style top stitches, select Overlock or Zigzag as its width needs to be adjustable. Without Width Property | Default (Single Needle) ---|--- Default Offset 0 Pick Stitch With Width Property | Overlock Zigzag Buttonhole Bar Tack * Ensure all of the Topstitch image files are located in the same path, as it will not be saved in the SST file properly. * The image is bigger than the actual size to prevent distortion in resolution when enlarging the image. * Drag and drop the saved SST file directly onto the Topstitch Item List or open it by pressing the Open button in the Property Editor. Adjust the property details such as the Length, Offset, Thread Thickness, or Color. ##
content_description: This webpage provides a detailed guide on how to register and save custom OBJ and texture files as Topstitch in the *.sst format within Marvelous Designer.

title: Buttonhole Style Window (ver. 2025)
content: ### Objective Add and organize Buttonhole style and apply it to the Buttonholes in the scene. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Style Tab (ver. 2025.0) Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Style Tab (ver. 2025.0) ### ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438074257177) ### ### Operation #### Open Asset Library 1. Open the Asset Library tab in Location. 2. Select the ![Asset Library.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438070272665) Asset Library icon to open the default location for Buttonhole assets in the New Library Window. #### Add New Buttonhole Style & Apply 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Click +Add at the top right. Or add a Buttonhole file by dragging it to the Buttonhole Style tab or on the Buttonhole asset. → A Buttonhole style is added. #### Copy Buttonhole Style & Apply 1. Click Copy at the top right. → A Buttonhole style is duplicated. 2. Replace an existing Buttonhole Style and apply it. Or after selecting a Buttonhole first, click the Assign Buttonhole to the right of the Buttonhole style. → The Buttonhole Style is replaced. #### Assign New Buttonhole Style 1. Select 1 or more existing Buttonholes in either the 3D window with the Select tool [Q] or in the 2D window with the select tool or Button/Buttonhole Select/move tool 2. While selected: go to the Buttonhole Style Tab 3. Select the Assign New Buttonhole option to generate and apply the New Buttonhole Style to all selected buttonhole assets. #### Buttonhole Item Context Menu Right-click a button in the location panel to rearrange the buttonhole list. **Menu** | **Description** ---|--- Delete | Deletes the selected Buttonhole style. ※Note: You can also delete them with the Delete buttonhole on the keyboard. A Buttonhole Style can only be deleted if there is no Buttonhole assigned to it. Delete All Unused Buttonholes | Removes unused Buttonholes from the Buttonhole list. Rename | Rename the Buttonhole style. Reset | Resets the properties of the Buttonhole style to the Default Buttonhole properties.

content: ### Objective Manage Trims as a shape or style in the Trim Window. It is possible to create, copy, apply, and set a style in the Trim list window. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Trim (Ver. 2025.0) Main Menu ▶ Object Browser ▶ Trim (Ver. 2025.0) ![ObjectBrowser-Trim.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438055259929) ### Operation #### Open Asset Library 1. Open the Asset Library tab in Location. 2. Select the Asset Library icon ![Asset Library.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438055387417) to open the default location for Trim assets in the New Library Window. #### Add & Apply one or more Trim Styles 1\. Click Add at the top right to load a file( .trm, .obj, .fbx or .zip)to use as Trim. or Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ/FBX/USD and import a file, In the popup window, choose Object Type as Trim. or drag and drop a file (from Library or File Explorer) directly to the Trim Style Window or 3D window. **→** A Trim style is added. 2\. Drag the style from the Trim window to the 3D window, apply it, and Glue. #### Copy Trim Style & Apply 1. Click Copy at the top right in the Trim Style window. → A Trim style is duplicated. 2. Drag onto an existing Trim Style and apply it. Or after selecting the Trim Style first, click the Assign button to the right of the Trim style. → The Trim Style is replaced. #### Change Trim Styles 1\. Use the Select/Move tool to select a trim in the 3D window. 2\. title: Show 2D Measurements (ver. 2025.0)
content: ### Objective Toggle on or off the option to see the distance that Internal tools, an internal lines or internal shapes are from edges of the 2D Pattern that it is within. ### Location 2D Display toolbar ▶ Information Display ▶ 2D measurements (ver. 2025.0) Line Property Editor ▶ 2D measurements (ver. 2025.0) Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 2D information ▶ Show 2D Measurements (ver. 2025) ※Note: * **This only works with measuring Internal Shapes & Internal Lines within a Pattern.** This will only show the mouse distance when you are using the internal Shape tools. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438121976345) ### ### Operation #### **Toggle on/off the view options:** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 2D information ▶ Show 2D Measurements (ver. 2025) 2D Display toolbar ▶ Information Display ▶ 2D measurements (ver. 2025.0) →Activated 2D distance measurements will show or disappear in the 2D window. #### **Use with Internal Shape tools** 1. Turn on the Show 2D measurements view options (see Location). 2. go to the 2D pattern Window ▶ 2D toolbar ▶ Internal Shape ▶Select any of the Internal Shape Tools (Internal Polygon/Line , Internal Rectangle, Internal Ellipse. or Dart). 3. Place the cursor over a pattern piece. →You will see the purple dashed lines and numbers that indicate the Cursor's distance to the 4 sides of a square pattern piece. (see image below) ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438072884505) (Image above shows the internal rectangle tool selected and 4 sets of purple dashed lines with numbers that indicate the Cursor's distance to the 4 sides of a square pattern piece.) ※Note: If you have no internal shapes in the scene or are on the wrong tools it will appear empty or that it does not work. Make sure to work within a 2D pattern and it will show. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438121976345) #### **Activate Internal Line or Shape's 2D Measurement Options.** 1. Turn on the Show 2D measurements view options (see Location). →All 2D distance measurements are deactivated by default. 2. Select an internal shape or Single internal shape/Line. 3. Go to the Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements **For Shapes** * * Expand 2D Measurements ▶ To Center * * Marvelous Designer calculates the distances from the Pattern outline to the center of the Internal Shapes/Lines. * Toggle on following options to activate the 2D measurements. Left, Right, Up, Down * Expand 2D Measurements ▶ to OUTLINE * * Marvelous Designer calculates the distances from the Pattern outline to the outline of the Internal Shapes/Lines. * Toggle on following options to activate the 2D measurements. Left, Right, Up, Down **For Internal Line / Segment points** * * Expand 2D Measurements ▶ To Center * * Marvelous Designer calculates the distances from the Pattern outline to the outline of the Internal Shapes/Lines. * Toggle on following options to activate the 2D measurements. Left, Right, Up, Down ※Note: * You can also apply the Internal Line options to an internal Shape's internal lines or segment point. * Adding, cutting, making modifications to an internal segment line will remove the measurements options and you will need to apply them again. * Selecting multiple lines or shapes does applies the operation to each individual asset they are not treated as a group.
content_description: This web page provides instructions on how to toggle and utilize 2D distance measurements for internal tools, lines, and shapes within a 2D pattern in version 2025 of the software.

title: Sculpt (Ver. 2025.0)
content: ### Objective Sculpt garments using various brush tools. ### Location 3D Window ▶ Sculpt Tool ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438037146393) ### Operation 1. Select Sculpt tool from the 3D Toolbar. The Sculpt dialog window will appear. 2. Select any Brush from the Brush toolbar. Check the brush Size and Focal settings when hovering over a 3D garment. 3. Adjust each attributes for each brush: Size, Focal, Realistic, Layer, Spacing, Depth 4. Click and drag on 3D garment to sculpt. Press Shift key on the keyboard while using any type of Brush tool to smooth out. 5. In Sculpt mode, the garment appears in gray by default. To change the garment's color during sculpting, enable the Custom Material option. When Custom Material is disabled, you'll see the garment's original texture. ### Brush Types ![Sculpt Wrinkle On.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438051249433) | Wrinkle | Left-click and drag to create wrinkles on the brush area. (ver. 10) ---|---|--- ![Sculpt Release On.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438116304537) | Release | Left-Click + Shift and drag to release wrinkles on brush area (ver. 10) ![Sculpt Sculpt On.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438037707161) | Sculpt | Emboss mesh. With invert option activated. engraves mesh. ![Sculpt Smooth On.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438037856025) | Smooth | Makes the surface flat on average. (Shortcut: Shift) ![Sculpt Grab On.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438100099097) | Grab | Moves vertices to express pulled surface. ![Sculpt Stamp O_n.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438038186649) | Stamp | Use an image as a stamp. ![Sculpt Pinch On.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438052527513) | Pinch | Close the position of the vertices, makes the surface sharper. ### Brush Property Depending on the type of brush, the properties you apply vary. Brush Property | Description | Brush Type ---|---|--- Wrinkle | Release | Sculpt | smooth | Grab | Stamp | Pinch Strength | Strength of brush. | X | X | O | O | O | O | O Size | Size of brush. | O | O | O | O | O | O | O Focal | Coverage of brush. (similar with Hardness) | O | O | O | O | O | O | O Spacing | Interval of brush. | X | X | O | X | X | X | X Depth | Depth of brush. | X | X | O | O | O | X | O Alpha | Using an image as brush. | X | X | O | X | O | O | X Invert | Change the direction of a brush. (shortcut: Alt) | X | X | O | X | O | O | X Realistic | Realistic (ver. 10) | O | O | X | X | X | X | X Layer | Layer (ver. 10) | O | O | X | X | X | X | X ### Option Custom Material | Allows assignment of a temporary material while the Sculpt Tool is activate. To maintain the Garment Rendering Style(e.g., monochrome, wireframe) from the 3D Window, disable this option. ---|--- Color | Specifies the color of the material. Roughness | Slider Adjusts surface roughness to control light diffusion. Metalness | Modifies reflection intensity to enhance the visibility of surface Curvature. Double Sides | Toggle on/off with Double Side option activated, apply custom material to both back and front side of mesh. #### **Using an Alpha Texture as Brush** 1. Click button next to Image. 2. Click an Image from default images. \- Focal setting is not available for image brush. 3. Click & Drag on 3D garment to Sculpt. \- Click & Drag to adjust the size and angle for Stamp brush. 4. To turn off an image, click button and select Off. \- Focal setting appears on brush property after turning off image. #### **Adding Alpha Texture** 1. Click ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438038474137) button next to image. 2. Select an image on the file browser. 3. Click & Drag on 3D garment to Sculpt. \- Click & Drag to adjust the size and angle for Stamp brush. 4. After adding image, can load the image by clicking button next to the image. #### **Show/Hide 3D Pattern (Shortcut Shift + Q)** 1. Show selected pattern only \- Select a pattern while input Shift + Q, other patterns will be hidden. 2. Reverse selected pattern/hidden pattern \- After operating no.1 above, click on the selected pattern while input Shift + Q to reverse hidden pattern/ selected pattern. 3. Adding hidden patterns \- To hide additional patterns, click on a pattern which you want to hide while input Shift + Q. 4. Show All 3D Patterns \- Click on the background while input Shift + C (Shift + Q for Ver. 2024.2 and below) to show all pattern.
content_description: Learn how to effectively sculpt garments in 3D using various brush tools and settings within the Sculpt Tool in Marvelous Designer.

title: Schematic Render (Ver. 2025.0)
content: ### Objective View 3D Garments with outlines and details shown in a format similar to that of flat fashion sketches or stylized 2D sketches. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Render ▶ Schematic Render 3D Window ▶3D Display Render Options ▶ Schematic Render ### Operation 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location above. → Render the 3D garment according to the schematic format. 2. Set the following options as needed. Option | **Description** ---|--- **Line Thickness** | Show or hide the silhouette line (the outline of the area where the garment and the background meet and the line of the wrinkled area inside the garment), Seamline, Internal Line and Topstitch line and adjust the line thickness. **Topstitch** | **(ver 2025.1)** Set specifications of Topstitches to achieve a visual appearance in the Schematic Render. 1. Click the Topstitch in Topstitch tab of the Object Browser. 2. In the Property Editor, activate the **Local Schematic Scale** option by clicking the checkbox. 3. Set the Topstitch parameters that appear below. * **Length** : Adjusts the length of each thread. * **Spacing** : Defines the spacing between each thread. * **Offset** : Adjusts the distance of the stitch from the edge of the applied line. * **Thickness** : Controls the visual thickness of the stitch thread. * **Width** : Sets the width of the stitch(especially Class 500 & 600 stitches). * **Distance** : Defines the distance between each stitch line. **Line Color** | Adjust the Color of the line. **Garment** | **Color** | Adjust the Color of the garment. **Texture** | The applied texture can be viewed as is. **Brightness** | Adjust the Brightness of the garment.
content_description: Explore and customize 3D garments with detailed outlines and schematic render options for a flat fashion sketch appearance.

title: Edit Texture
content: ### Objective Modify the Fabric's grainline and location for individual Patterns, and texture image's rotation and size for individual Fabric. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Texture ▶ Edit Texture 2D/3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Texture ### Operation **Move** 1. Follow the indicated location above. 2. Click ▶ Drag texture image applied to Pattern with the left mouse button. → The selected texture image of the selected Pattern is now being moved. **Zoom In/Out** 1. Follow the indicated location above. 2. Select a Pattern to zoom in/out. → A Gizmo is now being activated at the top-right corner of the 2D window. 3. Click ▶ Drag the diagonal line. 4. Enlarge or reduce the size of the selected texture image. → The selected texture image is now being adjustable while maintaining its horizontal and vertical ratios. 5. Click ▶ Drag the horizontal line in order to enlarge/reduce the texture image to up/down and left/right. → All texture images applied to the same Fabric are now being adjustable corresponding to the axis direction. 6. Alternatively, select a Fabric and enter the image's Width and Height value in Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Texture Transformation. → The width and height of all texture images applied to the same Fabric are now being adjusted. **Rotate** 1. Follow the indicated location above. 2. Select a Pattern to rotate the Fabric. → A Gizmo is now being activated at the top-right corner of the 2D window. 3. A circle appears when mouse-over the curve. 4. Drag around the circumference of the circle. → The selected texture image of the selected Pattern is now being rotated. **Rotate Grainline** 1. Follow the indicated location above. 2. Click on a Pattern to rotate its grainline. → The selected Pattern's grainline is now being in black color. 3. Drag around the activated grainline, when the mouse cursor becomes in a shape of circular rotation. → The selected grainline is now being rotated and so as the texture image. 4. Alternatively, select a Fabric and enter the angle value for grainline in Property Editor ▶ Fabric ▶ Grain Direction. → The selected grainline is now being rotated and so as the texture image. 5. Simulate once it is adjusted. → The draping is now being adjusted according to the change in grainline. **Align Grain Parallel to Selected** 1. Follow the indicated location above. 2. Select a Pattern to rotate its grain. → The grain of the selected Pattern is activated. → When multiple Patterns are selected, only the last Pattern's grain is activated, but the configuration is applied to all Patterns. 3. Right click on the Pattern and select Align Grain Parallel to Selected. →All selectable segments are highlighted. 4. Hover the mouse over the segment which the grain is to be aligned with. → The segment is highlighted in light blue. → The grain rotates. → When the selected segment is a curve, the grain rotates based on a line connecting the ends of the curve. 5. Click the desired segment. → The grain rotates parallel to the selected line. → When multiple Patterns are selected, all their grains rotate accordingly. **※ Note:** After selecting a Fabric, navigate to Property Editor ▶ Material ▶Transformation ▶Texture to type in the texture's width, height, and angle. Right-click to input the exact values while rotating textures and grainlines. Edit back of texture when you change Garment Rendering Style as Back Texture Surface (ver. MD10)
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for modifying the grainline and position of fabrics, as well as adjusting the rotation and size of texture images for individual patterns in a 2D/3D design environment.

title: Auto Sewing (Ver. 2025.0)
content: ### Objective Patterns are automatically sewn based on their placement on default avatars. ※Note: The available range of automatic sewing is as follows, * Top (T-shirts, Jackets, Jumpers, etc.)**** * Pants * Skirts ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Auto Sewing 3D Toolbar ▶ Auto Sewing ### Operation 1\. Click the Arrangement Points of the Avatar to arrange the Pattern. * Since Auto Sewing is calculated based on the information provided from the Arrangement Points make sure to place patterns on the correct arrangement points. **※ Note:** correct Arrangement Points should be used based on the rules below. Otherwise, Auto Sewing may not work properly. Collar/ Band | Use Arrangement Points at the Avatar's neck. ---|--- Bodies | Use Arrangement Points on the Avatar's body. Sleeves | Use Arrangement Points at the Avatar's arm, the cuffs can be used either arm/wrist Arrangement Points. Bottom | Use Arrangement Points at the legs. ※Note: Be mindful of arranging the pieces to auto-sew correctly. \- If the belt length includes a placket that is placed over the zipper, arrange the placket piece. \- Trace the internal line of the side pocket along the side seams. \- If the pants' width is large, arrange front and back pattern pieces separately by using each of the arrangement points. 2\. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. * Choose Garment type. (Top, Pants, Skirt) * For Tops: choose Front type from "Openable, Partially Openable, or Closed" * For Tops with "Closed" selected: choose "Collar seam". (Auto, Center Front, or Back Left) * Click OK. * The arranged patterns are automatically sewn. **※ Note:** * This feature will only work with the Default Bounding Volumes provided by Marvelous Designer, custom Bounding volumes & arrangement points will not work. * If sewing has been applied prior to automatic sewing, it is maintained while the rest of the sewing lines are being additionally auto-sewn. * Darts and Pleats can be sewn automatically without arranging patterns. * For Pleats, automatic sewing is possible only when Internal Lines are defined by the fold direction of the Pleats. * (Make sure your sewing line has segment points dividing the line for this operation to function properly)
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to utilize the Auto Sewing feature for efficiently arranging and sewing patterns on default avatars in Marvelous Designer.

title: Set Fabric Textures
content: ### Objective Represents the pattern or texture of the fabric. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ### Operation 1. Click the menu at the indicated location. 2. Select a fabric item. → Fabric properties appear in the Property Editor. 3. Set the basic material by referring to the table below. #### PBR (Default) Option | Description ---|--- Texture Repeat Type (Ver. 10) / Texture Mapping (Ver. 11) | Repeat | Repeatedly display the texture on the pattern. Unified Map | Display the texture based on the pattern layout of the UV map. [Repeat UV Settings] * Repeat U: Size the texture based on U direction. * Repeat V: Size the texture based on V direction. The number 1 means that the texture is repeated once between 0-1 of the UV map. Type | Set the appropriate Material Type. ※Note: If garment is created in Marvelous Designer or Downloaded from CONNECT, the fabric type may display as * (Read-only) Fabric Type with the same name in Marvelous Designer. However, since there is no render engine in Marvelous Designer, the fabric display in 3D window will not be accurate. Base Color (ver. 2025.0) | Color | Select your chosen color from the color wheel or leave as (None) Base Color Map | Recolor | Remove the default color to apply other colors while retaining the pattern or texture. Desaturate | It desaturates the color of the graphics. Set the Shadow Intensity and Shadow Brightness. Switch | Easily and quickly switch the color of solid fabric to a new one without losing the accuracy of the chosen color. ![Switch Color.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358364190105) ※Note: For consistent results, the Base Color Map should contain 1 color. If the Base Color Map contains multiple colors, users may experience unexpected or unintended results. Texture | Click the explore button and apply a texture image from Library/Folder ※Note: Click both back and side tabs and deactivate 'Use Same Materials as Front' to apply different materials to other faces of the pattern. Remove Texture Color | Remove the default color to apply other colors while retaining the pattern or texture. Normal Map | Apply Normal Map image to express uneven texture more realistically. Automatic | When a texture is applied, Normal Map is generated by adjusting the Intensity. Higher intensity makes the embossed detail raised off the surface, the lower intensity makes the details lower than the surface. Manual | Click the explore or apply the Normal Map image from the Library/Folder ※Note: Use the normal map image made with the exclusive tool to achieve an accurate normal effect. Also, add a normal map that is different with texture in order to create an extra pattern of surface. Displacement Map (ver.11) | Express thickness or bumpiness of fabrics or textures. As displacement maps are grey-scaled, their height is determined by the level of darkness of the grey color. ※ Note: * Increase the image resolution and apply the Gaussian Blur effect to express the texture smoothly. * Displacement map's minimum particle distance value is now 0.01 mm to allow for greater mesh density for displacement map (Ver. 2024.1) Amount | Adjust the maximum height of the displacement map. The white area of the displacement map shows the maximum height. Shift | Adjust the distance between the displacement map and the garment surface Clipping | Adjust to delete all geometries below the Clipping value. Particle Distance | Adjust the Particle Distance of newly created meshes. ※ Note: As more memory is used for lower Particle Distance, it is recommended not to set the Particle Distance below 1 for a wide area. Keep Continuity | Extend the adjacent face to eliminate the boundary line. ※ Note: Only applicable to Welded OBJs. Color | Express each of the fabrics in various colorways Opacity | Adjust Opacity to create sheer fabric. ※Note: When you apply opacity to texture, change Garment Rendering Style as Thick Textured Surface. Alpha Map (ver. 10) | Express level of transparency using a grayscale image map RGB Mode | The encoded map with alpha value in RGB channel. Alpha Mode | The encoded map with alpha value in alpha channel. Roughness | Intensity | Edit fabric gloss by adjusting Intensity of the Roughness Map | Edit fabric gloss by adding and modifying Roughness Map. Map | Select the Browse button next to the Map option to add a Roughness Map to the selected Fabric style. Map Intensity | Adjust the Map's Intensity. The range of Roughness map intensity was enlarged in (ver. 2024.2) Invert | Select to invert the gloss of the fabric. When this option is selected, the shinny part becomes dull and vice-versa. To use Specular Maps provided in below ver. 6, check this option. Reflection Intensity | Greater the Reflection Intensity value is, more reflective than the material or fabric is and vice-versa. Metalness (ver. 10) | Adjust metallic level. Higher value makes the surface more metallic. Metalness Map (ver. 10) | Partially express metallics using a grayscale image. The white parts of the map appear metallic. ※Note: * When working with Metalness Map, control Roughness Intensity and Reflection Intensity level that are suitable for the metallic texture. (e.g. Roughness Intensity 10, Reflection Intensity 90) * For the non-metallic areas(matte), assign the same metalness map to Roughness Map, and turn on Invert. #### Substance (ver. 10) Set the file format as Substance at the right menu of Material, you can use SBSAR file of Substance which is the main application of physical based rendering. To get a better rendering result for substance materials, enable High-Quality Render on 3D window. Properties | Description ---|--- Substance File | Import SBSAR file by clicking 'Explore' or, download SBSAR file by clicking 'Go to Substance Source'. * SBSAR file can be imported by Object Browser> Right-click on Fabric item. Preset | Choose the preset of SBSAR. Resolution | Adjust the image resolution of SBSAR. Custom Properties | Edit the properties of SBSAR. ※Note: Custom Properties are different depending on the property of the file. Refer to the [Substance Manual](https://docs.substance3d.com/home) for more detailed information. ※ Note: * Clicking on a Fabric from the Fabric List is going to highlight the Patterns where the Fabric is being applied to, in the 3D/2D window. * Clicking on a Pattern in the 3D or 2D window is going to highlight the Fabric where it is being applied to, in the Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab.
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive guidance on selecting and customizing fabric textures and properties within the Object Browser's Fabric Tab.
